CP-1.analysis_md:
The canonical record answers the reader question with audited annual and unaudited interim figures: FY2025 net revenues were 11,486 and Adjusted EBITDA 3,624, H1 2026 revenue rose 2.8% to 5,863 while Adjusted EBITDA fell 1.7% to 1,807, and in Q2 revenue grew 3.0% while Adjusted EBITDA fell 3.7% to 920 [C140, C133, C141, C142]. LTM Adjusted EBITDA to 30 June 2026 is 3592 and face debt 11807, so total leverage is 3.29x (calc: total leverage on face debt = 11807 / 3592 = 3.29x) [C132]. USD millions throughout; confidence is Restricted.

RBOT counts debt at face principal because the facility register is built from the debt note: 11,905 at 31 December 2025 and 11,807 at 30 June 2026. Balance-sheet carrying debt is lower, at 11,699 on the same date after discounts and deferred finance charges, so the two measures are not interchangeable [C130, C131, C132]. The GLPI and VICI financing obligations of 13,157 sit outside debt, and the filing estimates about 1.4 billion of 2026 lease payments to them, so debt-only leverage understates fixed claims [C143].

Reported EBITDA is operating income plus D&A, and Adjusted EBITDA adds back impairment, transaction costs and stock-based compensation. That bridge closes exactly in every column, for example 3,275 plus 349 of add-backs gives 3,624 for FY2025 [C133]. Segment history shows the mix shift: Las Vegas revenue fell to 4,049 in FY2025 while Regional held at 5,756 and Digital grew to 1,408; in Q2 2026 Regional rose to 1,570 and Las Vegas fell to 1,017 [C144, C145]. For creditors this is uneven cash generation, and one segment's strength should not be read as consolidated deleveraging without cash-flow confirmation.

Operating cash flow was 1,302 in FY2025 and 675 in H1 2026, against property and equipment purchases of 805 and 335 [C136, C146, C137, C147]. Cash interest paid for debt was 813 in FY2025 and 368 in H1 2026, with a further 1,349 and 686 of lease cash on the financing obligations [C134, C135]. Quarterly cash flows are not disclosed for Q2, so quarterly cash conversion is not established. Customer deposits and deferred revenue of 545 at 30 June are a funding float, not debt [C148].

What would change this view: sustained segment EBITDA, disclosed covenant headroom and debt reduction would strengthen it; lower H1 EBITDA, large lease commitments and the absence of any post-June reporting hold it back. The Alberta launch on 13 July 2026 is a subsequent event and is excluded from Q2 figures [C149]. Confidence in this module: Medium-Low.

CP-1A.analysis_md:
Four facts matter most to a creditor. Caesars is a large, lease-heavy and gaming-led operator whose Las Vegas segment is weakening while Regional grows partly through the Windsor consolidation; it has agreed to a US$31.00 cash take-private by Fertitta Gaming Holdco that is conditional and still pending, and the size of the new debt is not stated in the sources. [C78, C79, C52, C67, C80]

Operating model. FY2025 net revenue was US$11.486bn, led by casino at US$6.617bn, with hotel US$1.945bn, food and beverage US$1.714bn and other US$1.210bn. H1 2026 revenue rose to US$5.863bn from US$5.701bn while Adjusted EBITDA fell to US$1.807bn from US$1.839bn. For creditors, hold, visitation, labour, taxes and rent decide how much revenue reaches cash. [C81, C82, C83, C84, C85, C86]

Transaction and ownership. The signed agreement keeps Caesars as a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent after the merger. The Carano family, with about 5%, rolls part of its stake. A US$200m company termination fee and a US$450m reverse fee apply in defined cases, and Parent's financing is not a closing condition. Funding terms, schedules and post-close capitalisation are not in the pack, so no closing probability is inferred and pro forma leverage rests on the three synthetic tranches of this test run. [C52, C87, C88]

Governance view: Medium and incomplete. Reporting is audited and regular, and no repurchases were made in H1 2026, but acquisitions, a US$229m 2025 buyback and a small related-party lease are monitored items. [C63, C64, C89, C90]

Ratings: the pack shows issue ratings only, from FINRA (Moody's B1 and S&P BB- on the secured 2032s, Caa1 and B- on the unsecured 2032s). The corporate family rating B1 negative and S&P BB- on CreditWatch negative in the register are synthetic test values, marked as such, because no agency report was supplied. The downside path is a merger delay or weaker Las Vegas trading consuming cash while debt service and rent persist; the disclosed US$10m of merger costs is the first visible cost. [C80, C91]

Caesars is a geographically diversified gaming and hospitality company founded in 1973 by the Carano family. At 30 June 2026 it owned, leased, managed or branded 54 properties in 20 jurisdictions in North America, with about 53,800 slot machines, 2,800 table games and 46,300 hotel rooms. Gaming-led, discretionary revenue makes EBITDA and cash conversion cyclical.
